prompt.en: How does understanding opportunity cost improve the quality of economic decision-making? Illustrate with an example of a decision by a person, a company or a government. (3 marks)

label.en: Explains that it forces decision-makers to weigh alternatives deliberately instead of choosing blindly

level1.en: Before picking one option, what should a careful chooser line up next to it?

clue.en: When you name the option you give up, you compare at least two options before you choose.

level2Template.en: It makes the decision-maker compare the chosen option explicitly with ___ before committing resources.

label.en: Notes that it surfaces the invisible cost — what is forgone — rather than only the money paid

level1.en: Meera paid ₹500 either way, yet she still gave something up. What did the money not show?

clue.en: The price is easy to see; the option given up is not. Seeing both helps you choose well.

level2Template.en: It also exposes the ___ cost of every choice, namely the benefit forgone from the best alternative.

label.en: Gives a concrete example of wiser allocation — by a person (spending vs saving time/money), an enterprise (which product to fund) or a government (which project to build)

level1.en: Name one decision you know — pocket money, a factory budget, a government project — and show what comparing the forgone option would change.

clue.en: A farmer weighing barley against wheat, a family weighing a gadget against savings, a state weighing highways against hospitals — all decide better once they think about the option given up.

level2Template.en: For example, the ___ that thinks about the value of the option given up allocates money, time and land more wisely.

text.en: An understanding of opportunity cost improves the quality of economic decisions in several ways.
It makes the decision-maker compare the chosen option explicitly with ___ before committing resources.
It also exposes the ___ cost of every choice, namely the benefit forgone from the best alternative.
For example, the ___ that thinks about the value of the option given up allocates money, time and land more wisely.
